text:
matt-cs: Heads-up — ACME reported that their quantized endpoint (fp8/4bit combo) is ~2x slower than their fp16 baseline after yesterday's rollout. They hit p95 regressions and higher tail latency. Starting thread to coordinate triage.

ana-eng: ack. do we have logs or customer repro? any recent kernel changes rolled?

matt-cs: Customer repro attached in the ticket: small prompt sizes (~30 tokens), high concurrency (30rps), lots of short-lived sessions. They say fp16 was ~85ms p95, now fp8 is ~180ms.

kevin-runtime: interesting — those workload characteristics (short seq, many concurrent calls) can trigger suboptimal kernel selection + kv-cache churn. I pulled traces from their tenant in prod for the last 3 hours.

kevin-runtime: profiler snippet (reduced):
```
# per-request timeline (fp8 path)
queue_wait: 2ms
kernel_exec: 110ms
kv_lookup: 45ms (miss rate ~22%)
batch_unpack: 18ms
total: ~180ms
```

ella-platform: kernel_exec 110ms is the killer. FP8 kernels should usually be faster. Any evidence we're picking an emulation/slow kernel?

kevin-runtime: yes — kernel selector picked the "mixed-quant-fallback" path repeatedly. Heuristics pick different matmul kernels depending on batch size and seq_len. With many small batches we often fall back to a more portable kernel that avoids special tiled code; for fp8 our fallback isn't optimized for short sequences.

olivia-ps: is this related to kv-cache layout? If misses are 22% we might be thrashing due to small prefixes and evictions. customer uses many ephemeral conversations.

kevin-runtime: exactly. mvn profiler shows frequent KV shard reallocation when batch size spikes briefly. Small batches + aggressive shard compaction => cache churn, extra copy work, and triggers fallback kernel path because we break the contiguous kv stride assumptions.

matt-cs: Customer asks for immediate mitigation. What's safest short-term? revert quant rollout? pin to fp16? patch config?

ana-eng: short term options ranked: 1) Route that customer's requests to fp16 variant (simple routing rule) — fastest to reduce pain. 2) Increase KV cache capacity/disable compaction for tenant — may help but risk mem pressure. 3) Force kernel selector override to prefer short-seq fp8 kernel (if available) — requires canary and restart. 4) Rollback quantized model for that tenant.

kevin-runtime: I can push a per-tenant routing override to send ACME traffic to fp16 in 10-15m. I'll also capture a full perf trace and microprofile to reproduce locally.

ella-platform: please also add a conservative heuristic change: if seq_len < 64 and concurrency > 20, prefer tiled kernels for fp8 when available. We should test before flipping globally.

kevin-runtime: noted. I'll run a microbenchmark harness with their trace and test three kernel variants (fp16, fp8-optimized, fp8-fallback).

olivia-ps: I'll draft an update for the CS thread to tell ACME: temporary routing to fp16 while we triage, ETA 30-60m. Keep messaging: we expect no data loss, only routing. :white_check_mark:

sre-bot: deploybot: planned change: route tenant acme-prod -> model@fp16 for 1h (canary 5% -> 100%). Approved by kevin-runtime.

matt-cs: thanks team. Action items: Kevin - route to fp16 and run microbenchmark + post logs. Ana - validate memory impact if we increase kv capacity. Olivia - send customer note. Ella - spec heuristic tweak and test matrix. We'll regroup in 45m with findings.

kevin-runtime: quick preliminary numbers from local harness:
```
workload: short-seq/high-concurrency (from customer's trace)
fp16 p95: 82ms
fp8-optimized p95: 95ms
fp8-fallback p95: 178ms
kv-miss-rate: fp8-fallback ~20% (due to shard compaction)
```

kevin-runtime: conclusion: not all fp8 paths are faster. fallback path is dominated by kv/packing overhead. Optimized fp8 shows small improvement vs fp16, but selector sends some requests to fallback.

ella-platform: that's the smoking gun — kernel selector heuristics + kv compaction interactions. We'll need two follow-ups: (A) immediate selector override for short-seq customers (B) longer-term: make fallback kernel faster or improve selector accuracy.

olivia-ps: customer update sent: "We've routed your traffic to the fp16 model to restore latency while we investigate. No change to your prompts. We'll provide a full postmortem with actions."

matt-cs: agreed. Keep this thread for triage notes. I'll post the ticket link and timeline after the wrap-up. Thanks all.
